title: Latency-aware holdback and traffic-threshold protocol for safe auto-apply of batching/caching recs
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement a latency-aware, tiered holdback protocol for auto-applying Optimize suggestions (batching & prefix/KV caching profiles). The goal is safe, low-friction adoption that reduces customer unit cost without increasing user-facing latency or error rates. This ticket covers the orchestration layer: rollout gating logic, statistical canary evaluation, operator acknowledgement matrix, rollback triggers, and minimal console UI for approvals and visibility.
acceptance_criteria: New rollout controller can coordinate 3 holdback tiers (0.5%, 5%, 20%) and a full ramp in configuration
Canary evaluation runs synthetic and live traffic checks and rejects if 95th-percentile latency increases by >10% or error-rate delta >0.5% relative to baseline
Automated rollback triggers based on sequential hypothesis test (alpha=0.05) and telemetry windows are implemented
Operator UI shows active rollouts with per-tier telemetry and requires explicit acknowledgement for tier >5% unless admin override is enabled
Audit log entries created for each decision point (start, tier promotion, rollback, manual approve) and surfaced to Console and to customer-era logs for Private deployments
End-to-end e2e test harness exists and a GitHub PR with tests is merged
technical_notes: We will use a baseline window of 1h pre-rollout and 5m per-tier evaluation windows; these will be configurable per-customer
Canary uses both synthetic sampled requests (deterministic prompts) and live traffic sampling with traffic tag propagation
Sequential test chosen is a Wald's SPRT variant tuned for small effect sizes to allow early stop for regressions
Cost-savings evaluation is computed on cached token counts and average batching factor; we require >=3% expected token cost reduction before attempting autoapply

implementation_plan: Phase 1: Controller skeleton and tier config (0.5,5,20) + integration points for telemetry (2w)
Phase 2: Canary evaluator with synthetic+live sampling and sequential-stat test + console UI for ack (2w)
Phase 3: Adaptive windowing for low-QPS tenants + Dedicated opt-out mechanics (1w)
Phase 4: E2E tests, chaos scenarios, runbook update, and rollout (1w)
design_decisions: Decision: Use sequential testing (SPRT variant) for faster detection of regressions vs fixed-sample z-tests
Decision: Require both latency and error-rate checks; allow custom thresholds per-customer but default conservative values for hosted tier
Decision: Disallow autoapply for suggestions that change sequence-length behavior dramatically (e.g., prefetch >3x) without manual review
Decision: Persist rollouts as resources in control-plane DB with optimistic locking to prevent concurrent conflicting rollouts
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: False positives in low-traffic tenants can cause unnecessary rollbacks. Mitigation: adaptive windowing and min-sample requirements.
Risk: Subtle regressions in tail latency. Mitigation: combine synthetic deterministic prompts that exercise long-context codepaths with live sampling.
Risk: Operator overload if many rollouts fire. Mitigation: batch operator notifications and provide summary risk scores in Console.
Risk: Data privacy concerns in Private deployments. Mitigation: rollouts store only aggregated telemetry; raw traces remain customer-owned
